A specialist school for autistic children aged 3 to 14
Welcome to Hillingdon Grange School
Hillingdon Grange School is an independent, specialist school providing education and support to autistic children aged 3-14 and their families, which allows pupils to achieve their full potential in education and life.
Located over four sites, the school provides education from early years up to KS2 and offers a unique mix of education and support to pupils within a wide spectrum of needs and abilities. Personalised teaching and learning in an autism-specific environment allows pupils’ individual needs to be addressed completely and their capabilities fully realised.
Hillingdon Grange School actively promotes British Values of democracy, the rule of law, and the rights of the individual in the context of the tolerant and diverse society of modern Britain. We ensure that respect for both criminal and civil law is embedded in the curriculum and explicitly taught as part of the life skill of distinguishing right from wrong.
Hillingdon Grange School promotes principles which provide students with a broad general knowledge of public services, public institutions and the voluntary sector in England.
Our Curriculum
We offer opportunities for our pupils across four different sites accessing formal and non formal curriculum
Clinical Offer
We have a team of professional therapists, with specialist knowledge, training and experience in a range of psychological therapies.
Tour our school
Explore our setting across four sites.

pageCache.text:
Home Parents and Carers Referrals and admissions
Referrals and admissions
Criteria for Admission to Hillingdon Grange School
Procedures for Admission of Pupils
Parents may visit the school on designated open mornings.
The most effective route for admission is when parents and the Local Authority agree that Hillingdon Grange School may be an appropriate placement for a child and a joint application is made for assessment.
This involves the Local Authority contacting the school to request an assessment to determine whether Hillingdon Grange School would be an appropriate placement for the child.
The child and parents would then attend an Initial Contact Meeting at the school. The parent would bring a copy of the most recent reports (where possible) from the previous education provider to inform the meeting.
The school will then offer an assessment process, which is tailored to the young person’s individual needs. Following this assessment, the school’s referral and assessment team will meet to review the assessment. The Local Authority and parents will then be notified of the outcome of assessment via an assessment report.
If the school decides that it can meet the child’s Special Educational Needs and there is a suitable place available, the Local Authority will be asked to confirm that it accepts financial responsibility for the placement for the admission process to continue.
Following confirmation that the Local Authority will accept financial responsibility for the placement, a Transition Plan is developed by Hillingdon Grange School in consultation with the child’s parents, current school staff and other relevant professionals. Transition Plans are tailored to the individual needs of the pupil and include social stories to prepare the child for new routines and staff. A start date will be mutually agreed with Hillingdon Grange School, the local authority and parents.
© OFG Education 2026

Home Parents and Carers
Parents & Carers
The parents and carers of the children and young people we educate and care for are so important, and we take care to give them all the expert ongoing support they need at every stage of their partnership with us.
From the moment they make their first enquiry and right through the child or young person’s time in one of our schools, we’re there for them with tailored advice and support.
Tune in to Autism Unpacked, where we’re navigating SEN together through honest conversations, expert insight, lived experience and practical advice.
We’re joined by professionals from education and therapy, alongside parents, carers and people with lived experience, to share practical insights, explore the topics that matter and help families and those supporting children and young people feel better informed.
© OFG Education 2026

Home Parents and Carers Important Information
Important Information
We work closely with parents, carers, and other stakeholders to ensure that students’ targets and outcomes are met.
Before all students start, we ensure they have time to transition from school or other providers and complete a statement of need and baseline assessment.
Parent/ carer contact is crucial, and we ensure through various methods that parents are informed of progress such as daily Class Dojo updates, telephone calls, and termly pupil review meetings.
We also work closely with local authorities to ensure that Education Health Care Plan (EHCP) procedures are followed, and all appropriate parties are invited to EHCP annual reviews for input and contribution.
Tune in to Autism Unpacked, where we’re navigating SEN together through honest conversations, expert insight, lived experience and practical advice.
We’re joined by professionals from education and therapy, alongside parents, carers and people with lived experience, to share practical insights, explore the topics that matter and help families and those supporting children and young people feel better informed.

Home Our Approach Careers
Careers
Imagine Believe Do
Careers Vision Statement: Careers provision is not simply an opportunity, it is an absolute entitlement for all our students.
Links to important documents related to our Career Programme:
Our curriculum focuses on careers, and we provide our students with meaningful career-related opportunities and activities throughout their time at Hillingdon Grange School.
We are always looking to improve our provision and welcome feedback from students, parents, and carers. If you would like to give feedback, please click here: Parent Carer or Student Feedback
Provider Access Policy
We welcome the opportunity to welcome employers, Further Education settings and Training Providers into our School. Are you interested in being a partner with Hillingdon Grange School? If you would like to enquire about offering work experience placements or student talks, and mentoring, or showcasing your setting to our students, please do get in touch, we would love to discuss this with you! To do so, please contact Mitzi Smith, the EHCP & Transition Officer who works closely with OFG’s Future Programme in sharing information from student’s Transition Plans in order to the Futures Team to support the development of careers opportunities for our students as well as providing careers advice to our students yearly.
Thank you for your time, we are always looking to improve our provision and welcome feedback from training providers and employers if you would like to give feedback please click here: Training Provider or Employer Feedback

Home About Us What we do
What We Do
Hillingdon Grange School is a specialist school for children and young people aged 3-14 years, who have been diagnosed with Autistic Spectrum Conditions (ASC).
Hillingdon Grange School registered in 2025 as an independent Primary school, separate from Hillingdon Manor Secondary to provide a tailored Primary learning environment for Autistic children.
Located over three sites from early years through to the end of Key Stage 2 the school offers a unique mix of education and life skills support to pupils with a wide spectrum of needs and abilities. Personalised teaching and learning in an autism-specific environment allows pupils’ individual needs to be addressed completely and their capabilities fully realised.
Hillingdon Grange School is located across four sites to provide specialist education for children with autism from the age of three up to the age of 14.
The school is proud to offer an environment which inspires learning and where students can flourish, whilst personalised targets ensure every young person can make progress appropriate to their specific needs.
© OFG Education 2026
